subject: biology
title: The nitrogen cycle
key_idea: Plants need **nitrates** from the soil to make proteins. Bacteria move nitrogen between the air, the soil and living things. Farmers add nitrates with fertilisers, manure and crop rotation.

blocks.text: Plants cannot use nitrogen gas from the air. They take in nitrate ions from the soil through their roots.

items: Nitrates are used to make proteins (from amino acids) and chlorophyll.
Proteins are needed for growth, so more nitrate in the soil improves crop yield.
A low nitrate concentration in the soil gives poor plant growth.
Plants take up nitrates from the soil.
Nitrates are used to make proteins, which are needed for growth.

blocks.text: Four groups of microorganisms keep nitrogen cycling between the air, the soil and living things.

items.meaning: Bacteria and fungi that break down waste matter and dead organisms, releasing ammonia.
Bacteria that convert ammonia into nitrites and then nitrates.
Bacteria that convert nitrogen gas from the air into nitrates or ammonia.
Bacteria that convert nitrates back into nitrogen gas.

items: Some nitrogen-fixing bacteria live in colonies in **root nodules** on peas and beans. This is a mutualistic relationship.
Other nitrogen-fixing bacteria live in the soil.
Plants take up the nitrates. Animals get nitrogen compounds by eating plants or other animals.

diagram.alt: Sort each statement into the type of bacteria it describes: nitrogen-fixing, nitrifying or denitrifying.
diagram.prompt: Which bacteria does each statement describe?

items.text: Convert nitrogen gas into nitrates or ammonia
Live in root nodules on peas and beans
Convert ammonia into nitrites and nitrates
Make the nitrates that plants take up from decomposed waste
Convert nitrates back into nitrogen gas

items: Decomposers release ammonia. Nitrifying bacteria turn it into nitrates.
Nitrogen-fixing bacteria turn nitrogen gas into nitrates or ammonia.
Denitrifying bacteria turn nitrates back into nitrogen gas.

blocks.text: Crops remove nitrates from the soil as they grow. Farmers and gardeners replace them in several ways.

rows: Add nitrate compounds directly to the soil
Decomposers break down the waste and dead matter, so the nitrogen compounds return to the soil
A leguminous crop such as peas or beans is grown in some years. Nitrogen-fixing bacteria in its root nodules fix nitrogen gas from the air
Nitrogen-fixing and nitrifying bacteria make nitrates naturally

blocks.text: Crop rotation reduces the need to add nitrate fertilisers. Excess fertiliser can be washed into lakes and rivers, where it causes eutrophication.

items: Fertilisers, manure, compost and crop rotation all increase nitrates in the soil.
Leguminous crops have nitrogen-fixing bacteria in root nodules, so rotation reduces the need for fertilisers.

checks.q: Explain why increased nitrate levels in the soil improve crop yield.
checks.a: Nitrates are needed to make proteins (amino acids), which are needed for growth.

checks.q: Explain the role of denitrifying bacteria in the nitrogen cycle.
checks.a: They convert nitrates back into nitrogen gas in the atmosphere.

checks.q: Explain how crop rotation increases nitrate levels in the soil.
checks.a: Leguminous crops, such as peas or beans, are planted. They have nitrogen-fixing bacteria in their root nodules, which fix nitrogen gas from the air.

exam_phrases: nitrates are needed to make proteins / amino acids which are needed for growth
decomposers break down waste matter (into ammonia)
nitrifying bacteria convert ammonia / make nitrites / nitrates
nitrogen fixing bacteria convert nitrogen into nitrates
denitrifying bacteria convert nitrates back into (atmospheric) nitrogen
nitrogen-fixing bacteria live in colonies / root nodules on the roots

mistakes.wrong: Peas and beans produce nitrates, so they are used in crop rotation.
mistakes.right: "Produce nitrates" is ignored. Write that they have nitrogen-fixing bacteria in their root nodules, which fix nitrogen gas from the air.

mistakes.wrong: The bacteria live in the roots of pea and bean plants.
mistakes.right: "Live in the roots" is ignored. Write that they live in colonies or root nodules on the roots.

mistakes.wrong: Denitrifying bacteria make nitrates from nitrogen.
mistakes.right: Denitrifying bacteria convert nitrates back into atmospheric nitrogen. Making nitrates is the job of nitrifying and nitrogen-fixing bacteria.

mistakes.wrong: Eutrophication happens because nutrients build up in the water.
mistakes.right: "Nutrients" and "nitrogen" are ignored. Name the cause, such as fertiliser run-off or sewage, and say that nitrates build up in the water.

worked_example.question:
Nitrogen is cycled through the environment.

Describe the roles of bacteria in the nitrogen cycle.
answer_points: Decomposers break down waste matter, or dead organisms, into ammonia.
Nitrifying bacteria convert ammonia into nitrites and nitrates.
Nitrogen-fixing bacteria convert nitrogen gas into nitrates.
Denitrifying bacteria convert nitrates back into nitrogen.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each type of bacteria, with what it converts.

mistakes.wrong: Plant roots get nitrogen gas from compost in the soil.
mistakes.right: Plants cannot use nitrogen gas. Compost gives the roots minerals.

mistakes.wrong: Run-off brings nutrients into the lake.
mistakes.right: "Nutrients" is ignored. Write minerals, or name a mineral.
